$comment: Secrets never go on a command line. An argument is in the program's argv, which /proc/<pid>/cmdline shows to every process on the machine while it runs, so a token passed as -p/--password/--creds/--registry-password, or inside a user:$TOKEN@ URL, can be read by anything else on the build host. Hand it over on stdin instead (printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | podman login ... --password-stdin) or write it to a file (printf ... > file); printf is a shell builtin, so neither puts the value in any argv. Scans the Justfile (the whole file, comment lines skipped) and the run: scripts of every workflow, upstream-owned ones included. A value is secret-bearing when it references a variable whose name contains TOKEN, PASSWORD, PASSWD or SECRET (any case), or a ${{ }} expression that does (secrets.*, github.token). Evaluated by scripts/check-policies.mjs. See docs/security/SECURITY-AI.md.
